event.name: 17 November 2015 Lefkada, Greece, earthquake
event.tectonic_setting: Cephalonia Transform Fault Zone (CTFZ/CFZ), western Greece; predominantly dextral strike-slip rupture on southeast-dipping plane
event.region: Lefkada Island and adjacent offshore area, Ionian Sea, Greece

reference.title: Source characteristics of the 2015 Mw6.5 Lefkada, Greece, strike-slip earthquake
reference.journal: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth

inversion.method: MudPy joint kinematic inversion of three-component 1-Hz GPS, four strong-motion stations, and ascending Sentinel-1 InSAR LOS data. 2 x 1.5 km subfaults (480 patches), five 50%-overlapping triangular source-time windows, slip positivity, spatial and temporal smoothing; tested rupture speeds of 2.0-3.2 km/s, preferred 2.6 km/s. Figure 3a digitization after masking projected aftershocks and slip direction vectors.
inversion.green_function_model: Frequency-wavenumber elastic Green functions using the regional 1-D velocity model of Haslinger et al. (1999).
inversion.notes: FIGURE-DIGITIZED ESTIMATES, NOT ORIGINAL INVERSION COEFFICIENTS. Source: Melgar et al. (2017), Figure 3a, total-slip map, not the time-snapshot panels. The preferred inversion uses one 80-km plane (strike 20 deg, SE dip 65 deg) with 480 published 2 x 1.5 km subfaults (40 along strike, 12 along dip). The printed x-axis runs SOUTH (negative) at left to NORTH (positive) at right; the JSON along_strike_km coordinate runs from the southern end (0 km) toward the northern end (80 km). Therefore figure x_km = along_strike_km - 40; plot hypocenter is at x approximately 0. The plot vertical axis shows VERTICAL DEPTH, not down-dip distance. Patch down_dip_km is distance on the inclined plane from the assumed 0-km upper edge, and depth_km = down_dip_km*sin(65 deg), not a 1:1 copy of printed depth labels. Fig. 3a uses a continuous 0-1.6 m legend. Original PDF vector cell fills were calibrated to the legend. Green arrows (slip vectors), green hypocenter star, grey/black aftershock symbols, gridlines and other annotations were excluded from candidate pixel colors. Six cells wholly covered by symbols or ambiguous in the figure were filled from immediate neighbor values. A further four patches had sparse remaining direct figure color/background. A separate CSV accompanies the JSON with per-cell color support, obscuration and interpolation flags. The modeled main high-slip area is south of the hypocenter and concentrated at shallow depth, and the reported peak is about 1.6 m; digitized sampled peak need not equal the reported peak. The 0.01 m rounding conveys figure-color sampling, NOT true 1-cm inversion precision. Inversion allowed spatially variable rake between 135 and 225 degrees; patch-specific rake was not digitized or supplied by Fig. 3a. The patch rake_deg = 160 is a NOMINAL NOA CMT rake (quoted by the paper), not the inverted local rake, so treat the JSON as a scalar slip map. The paper reports hypocentral depth 10.7 km and an epicenter east of the fault trace but does not tabulate numeric coordinates; 38.6655 N / 20.6002 E are approximate NOA epicenter coordinates quoted independently by Papathanassiou et al. (2017), doi:10.1016/j.enggeo.2017.01.019, NOT digitized from Figure 3a. Upper-edge georeference location and geographic patch centroids cannot be established from the paper alone and are left null; geographic patch positioning must not be inferred from the epicenter. The model reports seismic moment 8.36e18 Nm (Mw6.54), a best-fit rupture speed of 2.6 km/s, duration approximately 17 s and moment-rate peak near 6 s. Slip average in summary_metrics is computed over all 480 sampled rectangles, including zero-slip cells; it was not published as a mean slip estimate.

provenance.compiled_by: Figure 3a vector-color digitization from uploaded Melgar et al. (2017) PDF; source-provided 40x12 subfault mesh; aftershock/slip-arrow masking; nearest-neighbor fill only for fully obscured cells
